label: SYNTHETIC READER: a test instrument, never a reader. Fictional; not evidence about the book; not readership.

findings.quote: If you only read one page, read this one.
findings.why: It tells the reader how to read and ranks the page for them before they have a reason to agree.

findings.quote: share one brief, one board and one hold
findings.why: A newsroom builder meets 'board' and 'hold' as bare jargon here, and nothing on the page says what a hold is or who may call one.
The steps never say what the editor's check or signature is, which is the control this reader most wants to see, so the formula reads as rubber-stamping.

findings.quote: Read it the whole way through, or take the short way
findings.why: A direction on how to read the book; the map and figure already offer the two routes.

findings.quote: **ruv-sgit:** I make the moving pictures in my workshop.
findings.why: A name with a hyphen and a dot-like feel, never explained, and nine hellos arrive before the reader knows why a cast exists.

findings.quote: the six alone through the morning
findings.why: The figure brief uses 'the six alone' as if known; it is only explained later, if at all.

findings.quote: There is one more thing I want you to see as you read.
findings.why: It directs the reader's attention instead of simply saying that the book is made the same way as the talk.

findings.quote: so you learn the convention once
findings.why: The two voices are already explained in prose at line 9, so a key card asks what the paragraph has answered.

findings.quote: Every one of them left a record of what it did
findings.why: A strong promise for a source-minded reader, but no pointer yet to where the record can be checked, which is what would earn trust.

findings.quote: At the other's next slot on the clock
findings.why: 'Slot' is used as settled vocabulary but is never explained, and 'session' and 'wake' appear loosely beside it.

findings.quote: It wrote a short letter, as a file
findings.why: A run of reporting sentences in the past tense with no 'I' and no hindsight, unlike the opening paragraph.

findings.quote: Asked at my slot. Answered at the researcher's. Used at my next.
findings.why: Four short sentences in a row, and the narrator's next paragraph then says the same thing again.
A string of fragments where one sentence could carry the thought, and it restates the request-needs-saying-once point already made at line 46.

findings.quote: the third of the three letters above, with its order of work
findings.why: This tells again the deck note and ruv-sgit's order that the three-letters scene gave in full thirty lines earlier.

findings.quote: One note followed, one not, and both are in the record.
findings.why: Three short clipped sentences close the paragraph; the useful point (an agent ignored housekeeping) could run as one.

what_holds: 00-start-here.md: five numbered steps at the top, in a friend's voice, that a builder could act on tomorrow.
00b-who-is-telling-this-story.md: the researcher 'who will not move without a source' and the promise that agents disagree with the editor on the page speak directly to a source-minded reader.
10-talking-through-git.md: the three quoted commit notes with times are exactly the record behind a line that this reader wants, and the ignored housekeeping note is an honest failure left in.
notes: As a would-be editor I looked in all three sections for where the editor signs and how a rubber-stamp is prevented; the formula says 'you check' but not what checking is. That is where I would not yet trust it. I would start with the researcher role if it is explained in a later chapter.
